meanings.note: needs 'не' with the verb: никто не войдёт

examples.trans: I know the town like nobody else.

examples.text: Садитесь и держите дверь. Никто не войдёт.
examples.trans: Sit down and hold the door. Nobody will come in.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates

Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to see', forming an aspectual pair with 'увидеть'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.
Secondary conversational sense ('? = see?') (drawing attention) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I can see the toy car.

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

examples.text: Ты видишь, сколько гостей сегодня вечером сидит в зале?
examples.trans: Do you see how many guests are sitting in the hall tonight?

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'пасной'). Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('spare').

examples.trans: Has anyone seen the spare key?

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'key', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: The white one? Give me the keys.

meanings.note: Coordinating or subordinating Russian conjunction meaning 'and', linking clauses in spoken dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('so, and what about') (starting a question: а жвачку?) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: нас = us (gen/acc/prep); у нас = we have, at our place
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Смотрите, какой у нас грязный унитаз!
examples.trans: Look, how dirty our toilet is!

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to know'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: emphasis: вот поэтому ты и... = that's exactly why you...

examples.trans: I was born and grew up here.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Coordinating or subordinating Russian conjunction meaning 'but', linking clauses in spoken dialogue.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо ещё.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need more.
I want to, but I can't.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'at all'.
Secondary conversational sense ('in general') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I have no idea at all.

examples.text: Я человек чистый. Я вообще не вор.
examples.trans: I'm an honest man. I'm not a thief at all.

meanings.note: usually in the genitive ничего, with не: ничего не осталось

examples.text: Ну что, очкарик? Видишь, ничего не осталось.
examples.trans: Well, four-eyes? See, there's nothing left.

meanings.en: to be able to, to manage to
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'мочь'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to be able', forming an aspectual pair with 'мочь'.

examples.trans: We came as soon as we could.
Will you be able to come tomorrow morning?

examples.text: Я думаю, что у меня есть мужчина. Он сможет меня защитить.
examples.trans: I think that I have a man. He will be able to protect me.

meanings.note: polite to one person, or to several people
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'мочь'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to help', forming an aspectual pair with 'помогать'.

examples.text: Экскаваторщик — это не мой уровень. Может, поможешь?
examples.trans: Excavator driver isn't my level. Maybe you could help?

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('my') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.
Agentive or instrument masculine noun meaning 'employee', declining across all six Russian grammatical cases.

examples.trans: He is an experienced company employee.
Why are you mistreating our staff?

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'терять'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to lose', paired with 'терять'.

examples.text: Что смотрите, бандерлоги? Вы совсем страх потеряли?
examples.trans: What are you staring at, you monkeys? Have you lost all fear?

meanings.note: Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('what a').

examples.text: Экая досада, мы забыли купить свежую мяту для коктейлей!
examples.trans: What a shame, we forgot to buy fresh mint for the cocktails!

examples.text: Экая невидаль — столик у окна заказали за неделю вперёд.
examples.trans: What a wonder — the table by the window was booked a week in advance.

meanings.note: Prefix 'до-' marks reaching a boundary or finishing the remainder of an action (stem 'сада'). Common feminine noun meaning 'annoyance / shame' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Экая досада, соус опять немного подгорел!
examples.trans: What a shame, the sauce burned a little again!

examples.text: От досады Макс громко хлопнул дверью холодильника.
examples.trans: Out of annoyance, Max loudly slammed the refrigerator door.

meanings.note: Expressive conversational Russian interjection or greeting ('oh') used directly in spoken exchanges.
Invariable Russian adverb used to modify verbs or whole clauses with the sense 'how'.
Secondary conversational sense ('as') (как вы знаете = as you know) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: adds emphasis to the word before it

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Secondary conversational sense ('there is, there are') (present есть; у меня есть = I have) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'at' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('I have') (possession) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('from (ask from someone)') (просить у кого) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Prefix 'вс-' ('up') marks upward or sudden onset of action (stem 'егда').

examples.trans: She's offended. She's always like that.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'duplicate' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Я всегда храню дубликат ключей от кабинета.
examples.trans: I always keep a duplicate of the office keys.

examples.text: Сделай, пожалуйста, дубликат этого важного документа.
examples.trans: Please make a duplicate of this important document.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to keep, to store', paired with 'сохранить'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to keep (a secret)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Where do you keep your money?
She keeps the caviar in the fridge.

examples.text: Она там взятки для врачей хранит.
examples.trans: She keeps bribes for the doctors in there.

meanings.note: Conversational Russian particle ('here') that adds modal nuance, emphasis, or discourse tone in spoken dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('! = you'll see!') (emphasis) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: All right, here you go. There, look.

meanings.note: accusative/genitive его (него after prepositions), dative ему (нему)
Secondary conversational sense ('it') (for masculine and neuter things) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

найтись.gloss: to be found, to turn up

meanings.en: to be found, to turn up
meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'йтись'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to be found', forming an aspectual pair with 'находиться'. The reflexive suffix '-ся'/'-сь' makes the action intransitive, reciprocal, or directed at the subject.

examples.trans: Say thank you that the dog was found.

examples.text: Опоздал ты, Аркаша. Другие люди нашлись.
examples.trans: You're too late, Arkasha. Other people came along.

meanings.note: the 'е' drops out in the other forms
Secondary conversational sense ('' ' = over and out') (radio and phone phrase) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: At the end of the film everyone is happy.
